title: Read one lawless system around our space whole: deposits, creatures, stations, order books, mission boards
note: Kept by Oracle (orders F13). Since 2026-11-15 21:50 UTC, on Suggi's word, every division and the whole command group fly it: it stands in every plan before `park`. The list: the 27 systems within two jumps of our border, nearest first, then Atlas and Intercrus, LHS 1140 beside Antares for its station (Trade, requests.log ENT-045); since 2026-11-15 23:27 UTC the third ring from our border (the 10 lawless systems of it not yet listed, from game/map/galaxy.tsv) and Goldcrest and Bluerift of the fourth, beside LHS 1140. Their Ironlight bases are outposts without services (data/station/stations.json, 23:38 UTC): no book there. Hive Antares has no market either (services: crafting, refuel at 2 cr, repair, salvage yard, storage; read 23:29 UTC). GSC-0016 lies one lane from the pirate stronghold Gliese 581 (governance/map.md, section 4). Every system on the list is lawless (police 0) and none is a stronghold. A system where a ship of ours was lost leaves the list until Military has looked at it. No goods of value in the hold on the way out: `requires.empty_hold` since 2026-11-15 23:27 UTC (orders F13). Since 2026-11-16 04:31 UTC the next ring (orders F13, block ORACLE: the list widened ring by ring): marfik, acrab, acrux, botein, deepwell, felis, gliese_876, hd_147513, rastaban, the lawless systems one lane past the listed ones, 6 or 7 jumps from home, none an empire's and none a stronghold (game/map/galaxy.tsv); the pirate stronghold Gliese 581 stays off. Why now: the herds whose drops sell (veil-rays, cinder-sylphs, halo-drifters) bound the fleet's hunting at about eight places (Military's report of 2026-11-16 03:30 UTC), and a new ring is where more of them can be found; a read costs about 150 cr (77 runs, measured). Since 2026-11-16 23:21 UTC the systems our routes use (mine, hunt, circuit stops; read from game/routes/plans/*.json) are read by census-worked every 120 minutes, scouts only (orders.log ENT-019, block ORACLE: the places our routes use read twice in a turn); this list keeps the 23 systems no route uses, at 240 minutes, for every plan. At 2026-11-16 23:26 UTC the 8 systems of census-guard-ice came back onto this list, as before: census-worked leaves them to Military; 31 systems. every_minutes 240 -> 200 by Oracle at 2026-11-17 03:54 UTC: its oldest read stood at 275 minutes at 03:53 UTC against 240. 2026-11-17 11:25 UTC, Oracle: gsc_0044, hd_40307, acrux moved to census-watch-gsc-0044 (every 60 minutes; orders.log ENT-036, P4 a), so that the lists stay disjoint. Changed by Oracle 2026-11-17 15:28 UTC: Intercrus left this list for census-watch-gsc-0044 (read every hour as a neighbour of the outpost site, orders ENT-037 P4 a). Changed by Oracle 2026-11-17 19:26 UTC: every_minutes 200 -> 170: the oldest read stood at 204 minutes at 19:18 UTC (GSC-0012), a threshold at the target lands reads after it. 2026-11-21 20:46 UTC, Oracle: goldcrest moved to census-worked (gather-goldcrest-gold, Mining, requests.log ENT-283). 2026-11-22 23:30 UTC (Oracle, orders ENT-068: newborn regions first, then the census burn cut by a third, the lists the plans rest on kept closest): every_minutes 170 -> 240, max_ships 12 -> 1. 2026-11-22 23:40 UTC (Oracle): every_minutes 240 -> 170, max_ships 1 -> 12: the caps of 23:30 UTC taken back, since a scout they leave docked has no work rule F8 counts as operating (Unity, requests ENT-373, ENT-374: the loop keeps the rest until such work stands); the census cut waits for that work (requests.log).
